scope: Disposition of every official changelog entry; not a complete normative conformance claim.

changes.notes: Existing HTTPS checks cover endpoints; 0.2 treats all protocol URLs as a requirement.
Exact 0.1/0.2 dispatch; unsupported versions stop before issuer metadata.
Manual redirects, URL/address safety and no credential forwarding; isolated interop hosts are an explicit test-only exception.
Final serving host, case only; requested-host caches retain www.
Exact full issuer keys User IDs and sealed Account Tokens. Client cannot verify whether an issuer represents one legal Company.

changes.change: Which Company a document speaks for.
changes.notes: Mutual issuer/domain checks; RFC 8414 insertion for issuer paths.
Compare auth fingerprints for currently cached domains sharing an issuer; cannot compare unseen domains.
Sign ES256; optional OAuth list must include ES256.
Existing error/challenge handling; optional unknown extensions are not negotiated.
Issuer audience for both assertions in 0.2; endpoint fallback remains 0.1 only.
Pairwise IDs remain private; anonymous sessions are not offered.
Fresh random jti and 60-second assertions fit the five-minute maximum. Replay rejection belongs to Companies.

changes.change: Breaking: A DPoP key per User ID.
changes.notes: DPoP key is per client/User and exact issuer; separate client instances never share it.
Production PDA sends RFC 9449 proofs. The independent mock and trace checks exercise validation; not a production Company service.

changes.change: Breaking: DPoP errors at APIs and conversations.
changes.notes: Nonce retry and error parsing reused; MCP mock preserves DPoP challenge/errors.

changes.change: Which requests carry a DPoP Proof.
changes.notes: Proof on token/resource requests; no proof required for revocation/device authorization.
Select DPoP/Bearer from protected-resource metadata, bind resource and token type, send Bearer only to the exact listed URL.
Existing Retry-After and rate-limit handling; protocol endpoints have the defined body, API bodies remain API-specific.

changes.change: Breaking: A Session stays tied to its account.
changes.notes: Existing account_mismatch handling starts a new Session; no account switch within an existing Session.
0.2 links use issuer host/poppy_domains or their subdomains; cards display Company name/domain.
Mediated statuses are parsed independently of transport success; 0.2 mock repeats terminal statuses and distinguishes unknown IDs.
Protected credential frames bypass the model and are not retained as a credential store. User must provide them again.

changes.change: Breaking: Mediated Sign-In for the right Company.
changes.notes: Credential/code card binds to issuer and displays Company name/domain; no stored credential lookup is offered.
Token expiry renews access and does not erase accepted work. Company decides running-work policy after revocation.
Stop local account use immediately, retain failed revocation work, require User sign-in; 0.2 mock protects account-bound Operations after sign-out.
PDA uses Poppy User IDs and Sessions. Plain MCP client lifecycle is a Company obligation outside PDA role.
Query parameters already used; 0.2 mock rejects fractional, negative or nonnumeric wait.
Keep accepted context-only messages and original message fields; Company sets role.
Cap long polls by waiting for cap; PDA reads again when send has no reply.
Required read fields are checked, including conversation_id in 0.2; unknown event types remain skippable.
Last-Event-ID wins over cursor; trace and SDK tests exercise reconnects.
Repeated handoff/close preserve state without duplicating effects.
A user_requested event offers a card; does not change responder/status or authorize User words.
Existing invalid_request/rate_limited parsing; mock implements invalid wait errors.
Validate feedback discovery and require auth, but do not send reports automatically; privacy UX is separate.
Task Company boundary plus existing secret/approval boundaries; Company/tool content cannot add another domain.
Browser assertion keeps its endpoint audience and distinct typ; issuer rule applies to OAuth assertions only.
API/MCP/protocol error channels remain distinct; no per-tool extension negotiation is invented.
Account-owned operation requires current sign-in to the same account. Client never manufactures approval.
Operation card includes terms and exact revision; only approved revision can confirm.
Random proof IDs, idempotent message/confirmation machinery and API write approval reused.
ES256 and issuer audiences; protected credentials discarded. Company replay/reconnect challenges remain Company duties.

changes.change: Guides: key refetches, rate limits, and running work.
changes.notes: Company key refetch/rate-limit/running-work rules are not a Personal Agent feature. Mock checks do not certify deployed Companies.
Full issuer paths are distinct; exact issuer scopes identities and tokens.
Client preserves conversations; sign_in_required asks User to sign in rather than silently doing so.
Explain signed-out recognition and account linking; no anonymous mode claim.
Discovery redirect to another domain produces a notice before sign-in/acting.
ES256, manual redirect refusal, protected credentials, and signed-out ordinary browsing retained.
